name: גִּדֵּל
gloss: he has brought up; or, great
summary: Two family heads in the lists of those who returned from Babylon: the sons of Giddel among the Nethinim (Ezr 2:47; Neh 7:49), and the sons of Giddel among the sons of Solomon's servants (Ezr 2:56; Neh 7:58; the two groups are totalled together in Ezr 2:58). The name has the form of the piel perfect of גָּדַל, “he has brought up, made great”, as in “who brought up (מִי גִדֵּל) these?” (Isa 49:21), probably with God understood as the subject.

evidence.note: “The sons of Jaalah, the sons of Darkon, בְּנֵי גִדֵּל.”
All the Nethinim and the sons of Solomon's servants together, 392.
The same form as a verb: מִי גִדֵּל “who brought up (these)?”

note: BDB's c.aq.ah also counts Isa 49:21, the piel verb; it is cited as evidence for the form only. The subject of the verb is not given in the name; “God has brought up” is a reading, not stated in scripture.
